statement.p: Show that \Phi(u,v)= (4 u+9 ,u-v,7 u+v) parametrizes the plane 2x-y-z=18. Then:
(b) Find the area of \mathcal{S}=\Phi(\mathcal{D}), where \mathcal{D}= (u,v) : 0\le u\le 9, 0\le v \le 2.
(c) Express f(x,y,z)=yz in terms of u and v and evaluate \iint_{\mathcal{S}} f(x,y,z)\,d \mathcal{S}.

static.solution:
x=4 u+9, y=u-v, and z=7 u+v satisfy the equation of the plane, 2x-y-z =2(4 u+9 )-( u-v )-( 7 u+v )=8 u+18-u+v-7 u-v=18 Moreover, for any x, y, z satisfying 2x-y-z=18,
there are values of u and v such that x=4 u+9,
y=u-v, and z=7 u+v, since the following equations can be solved for u and v: \begin{array}{rcl}x\amp {}={}\amp 4 u+9\\ \noalign{\smallskip} y\amp =\amp u-v\\ \noalign{\smallskip} z\amp =\amp 7 u+v\\ \noalign{\smallskip} 2x-y-z\amp =\amp 18\end{array}\quad\Rightarrow\quad u=\frac{x-9}{4},\quad v=\frac{x-9}{4}-y We conclude that \mathrm{\Phi }( u,v ) parametrizes the whole plane 2x-y-z=18.
(a) The tangent vectors {\mathbf{T} }_u and {\mathbf{T} }_v are: {\mathbf{T} }_u =\frac{\partial \phi }{\partial u}=\frac{\partial }{\partial u}( 4 u+9,u-v,7 u+v )= \left\lt 4,1,7 \right>{\mathbf{T} }_v =\frac{\partial \phi }{\partial v}=\frac{\partial }{\partial v}( 4 u+9,u-v,7 u+v )= \left\lt 0,-1,1 \right> The normal vector is the following cross product: \mathbf{n} ( u,v )={\mathbf{T} }_u \times {\mathbf{T} }_v = \left|\begin{array}{rrr}\mathbf{i} \amp \mathbf{j} \amp \mathbf{k} \\ 4\amp 1\amp 7\\ 0\amp -1\amp 1\end{array}\right|=\left|\begin{array}{rr}1\amp 7\\ -1\amp 1\end{array}\right|\mathbf{i} -\left|\begin{array}{rr}4\amp 7\\ 0\amp 1\end{array}\right|\mathbf{j} +\left|\begin{array}{rr}4\amp 1\\ 0\amp -1\end{array}\right|\mathbf{k}= 8 \mathbf{i} -4 \mathbf{j} -4 \mathbf{k} = \left\lt 8,-4,-4 \right> (b) That area of S=\mathrm{\Phi }(\mathcal{D}) is the following surface integral: Area(S)=\iint_{\mathcal{D}} \| \mathbf{n} ( u,v )\| \,du \,dv=\iint_{\mathcal{D}} \| \left\lt 8,-4,-4 \right>\| \,du \,dv= 4\sqrt{6}\iint_{\mathcal{D}} 1 \,du \,dv=
4\sqrt{6}\, \mathrm{Area} (\mathcal{D}) =4\sqrt{6}\cdot 9\cdot 2=72 \sqrt{6} (c) We express f( x,y,z )=yz in terms of the parameters u and v: f\left(\phi ( u,v )\right)=( u-v )(7 u+v )=7 u^2-6 uv- v^2 Using the Theorem on Surface Integrals we have: \iint_S f( x,y,z ) \,dS = \iint_{\mathcal{D}}f\left(\phi ( u,v )\right)\| \mathbf{n} ( u,v )\| \,du \,dv=\iint_{\mathcal{D}} \left(7 u^2-6uv- v^2\right)\| \left\lt 8,-4,-4 \right>\| \,du \,dv= 4\sqrt{6}\int_0^{2} \int_0^{9} \left(7 u^2-6uv- v^2\right) \,du \,dv=4\sqrt{6}\int_0^{2} \left( \frac{7 u^3}3 -\frac{6u^2v}2- v^2u\right)\bigg|_{u=0}^{9} \,dv= 4\sqrt{6}\int_0^{2} \left(\frac{5103}3-\frac{486v}2-9 v^2\right) \,dv =4\sqrt{6}\left(\frac{5103v}3-\frac{486v^2}4-\frac{9 v^3}3 \right)\bigg|_0^{2} =\frac{138816\sqrt{6}}{12}\approx 28335.7
